newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to launch satellite TV programme - papers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to launch satellite TV programme - papers.

text.p: Iraq's National Assembly has ratified a bill to set up a satellite television channel covering Arab and European countries, state-run newspapers said on Monday.
"Because the project is important in communicating Iraq's voice to the rest of the world, the National Assembly (parliament) ratified the bill setting up the new television channel," the papers said.
They said arrangements for the channel had already been made with the Paris-based European Eutelsat and it would be ready to operate at the end of the year.
The director of the channel, Feisal al-Yasiri, said Arabsat, of which Iraq is a member, had rejected a request to carry the programme because Baghdad had not paid debts.
Iraq is under stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, including a ban on oil exports.
The papers gave no further details on how Iraq would pay for the satellite or what kind of programmes would be broadcast.
